posts.text: ADHD in women is the art of overcompensating until you fall apart.
I stopped fighting my ADHD and started building around it.

Getting diagnosed as an adult feels like starting school over. Suddenly you're relearning things you thought you already knew about yourself. Why you were the disorganized one, the daydreamer, the one who tried so hard and still got called lazy. It's not just a diagnosis, it's a rewrite of your whole personal history. And that takes time to sit with. You're allowed to grieve the years you spent thinking something was wrong with your character instead of your wiring.
ADHD doesn’t mean I can’t focus—it means I can’t *choose* what to focus on. Anyone else?
Sometimes ADHD has 100 ideas before breakfast because the magic’s in the mayhem.
I once hyperfocused on rearranging my apps instead of doing my actual work.
